products.d.drag: Move freely, or snap to grid points 0.5 apart
products.d.proj: Which vector is projected onto the direction of the other
products.d.A: Components of a; drag its tip to change them
products.d.B: Components of b; drag its tip to change them
products.dot.goal.proj: Dot (scalar) product = magnitude of one vector × projection of the other: $\vec a\cdot\vec b = a\,(b\cos\varphi)$
products.dot.goal.comp: Magnitude-angle form $ab\cos\varphi$ = component form $a_x b_x + a_y b_y$
products.dot.obs.drag: Drag the tips of $\vec a$ and $\vec b$; drag the point on the graph to turn $\vec b$ at fixed length
products.dot.obs.sign: Sign: $0^\circ \le \varphi < 90^\circ$ → positive, $\varphi = 90^\circ$ → zero, $90^\circ < \varphi \le 180^\circ$ → negative (the projection points backwards)
products.dot.obs.perp: Perpendicular vectors: projection of length 0 → $\vec a\cdot\vec b = 0$
products.dot.obs.plot: Graph: $\vec a\cdot\vec b = ab\cos\varphi$ as $\varphi$ varies at fixed magnitudes; the point is the current value
products.dot.obs.panel: Σ panel: both forms with the current values, same result
products.dot.asm.plane: Both vectors lie in the $xy$ plane; one grid square = 1 (dimensionless components)
products.cross.goal.area: Magnitude of the cross (vector) product = area of the parallelogram the two vectors span: $\lvert\vec a\times\vec b\rvert = a\,(b\sin\varphi)$
products.cross.goal.dir: Direction perpendicular to both, by the right-hand rule: curl the fingers from $\vec a$ to $\vec b$, the thumb points along $\vec a\times\vec b$
products.cross.obs.drag: Drag the tips of $\vec a$ and $\vec b$; drag the point on the graph to turn $\vec b$ at fixed length
products.cross.obs.rhr: $\vec b$ counterclockwise from $\vec a$ → $\odot$ (out of the page); clockwise → $\otimes$ (into the page)
products.cross.obs.par: Parallel or antiparallel ($\varphi = 0^\circ$, $\pm 180^\circ$): zero area → $\vec a\times\vec b = \vec 0$
products.cross.obs.anti: Swapping the order flips the sign: $\vec b\times\vec a = -\,\vec a\times\vec b$
products.cross.obs.plot: Graph: $(\vec a\times\vec b)_z = ab\sin\varphi$, largest area at $\varphi = \pm 90^\circ$
products.cross.asm.sign: Both vectors lie in the $xy$ plane, so $\vec a\times\vec b$ has only a $z$ component. $\varphi$ is measured from $\vec a$ to $\vec b$, counterclockwise positive ($-180^\circ$ to $180^\circ$)
